title: Computation of the Storage Charge on a Retrofit Project
content:
# Computation of the Storage Charge on a Retrofit Project

The storage charge raised on equipment a building cannot yet receive, on a project under Equipment Replacement & Retrofit Projects, is worked out from the weeks the equipment has stood in storage, the weekly storage rate the project carries and the free period the owner is allowed.

## The quantities

1. **The storage clock.** The storage clock runs from the day the equipment arrived, taken from the most recent delivery on the project recorded as having been stored because the site could not receive it.
2. **The weeks in storage.** The weeks in storage are the whole weeks begun between the day the storage clock runs from and the day the charge is raised, a part week counting as a whole week.
3. **The free period.** One week of storage is free.
4. **The weekly storage rate.** The weekly storage rate is the project's weekly storage charge, the weekly figure its class carries.
5. **The weekly charge for the lot.** The weekly charge for the lot is the weekly storage rate as it stands.
6. **The weeks charged.** The weeks charged are the weeks in storage less the free period, and where that difference falls below zero no charge is raised.
7. **The charge.** The storage charge is the weeks charged multiplied by the weekly charge for the lot, and that product is rounded to the nearest cent.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

| Day the equipment arrived | Day the charge is raised | Days between | Weeks in storage | Free period | Weeks charged | Weekly storage rate | Storage charge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| the 1st | the 26th of the same month | 25 | 4 | 1 | 3 | USD 195 | USD 585 |
| the 1st | the 8th of the same month | 7 | 1 | 1 | 0 | USD 195 | USD 0.00 |
| the 1st | the 9th of the same month | 8 | 2 | 1 | 1 | USD 225 | USD 225.00 |

In the first row, 25 days begin a fourth week, so the weeks in storage are 4; less the free week, 3 weeks are charged, and 3 weeks at USD 195 come to USD 585.00. In the second row the weeks in storage equal the free period, the weeks charged are nought and no charge is raised.

## Points of judgement

**A lot that arrived eight days ago.** Eight days have begun a second week, so the weeks in storage are 2. One week is free, so one week is charged.

**A lot that arrived three days ago.** Three days are part of the first week, which counts as a whole week; the weeks in storage are 1 and the weeks charged are nought, so nothing is raised.
